detail.longDescription: Y'all still haven't figured out that ... 1. It's not the query that is triggering the AI summaries 2. The LLMs are using multiple search engines/indexes 3. The LLMs are using different search systems 4. Every time an LLM "grabs content" from a site represents a proxy visit 5. There is no "AI visibility" without search results 6. You need to be trusted by BOTH the search engine AND the LLM as a reliable source 7. All your correlation studies are worthless pseudo-analysis 8. Every searcher or AI user has their own constantly evolving context 9. AI apps and chatbots are remembering what their users ask them, search for, and say in reply -- all of which alters the users' contexts 10. The AI platforms are not the models 11. Any AI platform or search engine may use more than one model in response to a query 12. Search queries ARE prompts to AI-enhanced search engines 13. Your Javascript-based analytics (especially GA 4) are missing most of the traffic coming to your sites. 14. You cannot design an AI agent that will reliably perform a sophisticated task (because "AI makes mistakes" and you're providing no intervention or oversight once the agent starts running) 15. LLMs follow links even if you don't see them following links # ai # seo # google # gemini # chatgpt # perplexity # claude # searchengines # llms
